sources.entry: shallow-backup - Easily create lightweight documentation of installed applications, dotfiles, and more.

summary.one_liner: shallow-backup is a command-line tool that creates lightweight backups of installed packages, apps, fonts, and dotfiles and can push them to a remote Git repository.
summary.what_it_does: It backs up dotfiles and dotfolders from where they live on the system, plus app config files (VSCode, Sublime Text, Terminal.app), installed package lists (brew, cask, cargo, gem, pip, npm, macports, VSCode extensions, Sublime packages, system applications), and user-installed fonts. Files are copied rather than symlinked, and reinstallation from the backup directory is described as idempotent. Behavior is controlled by a JSON config file that lists which dotfiles to back up, gitignore rules, and a config_mapping for app configs. Each dotfile entry can have optional backup_condition and reinstall_condition expressions evaluated with bash. It is git-integrated, can use a nested dotfiles repo as a submodule, and offers both an interactive mode and command-line flags for scripting.
use_cases: back up dotfiles from home directory
record list of installed Homebrew and npm packages
restore dotfiles on a new machine
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd shallow-backup && pip3 install .
notable: Copies dotfiles from their live locations instead of symlinking them
Conditional backup and reinstall using bash expressions per dotfile
Git integration with a trufflehog pre-commit secret scan (v6.2+)
Can track a separate dotfiles repo as a git submodule
Every interactive feature is also available as a command-line flag
caveats: Config files can execute code via condition expressions, so the config should not be writable by untrusted users and the tool should not be run with elevated privileges
Requires pre-commit and trufflehog as dependencies, which must be installed separately
Several app-config and package features are specific to macOS apps and tools such as Terminal.app and Sublime Text
